claim: Aim24 exhibits the same distribution as the subunits of the MICOS complex in a proteomics screen for proteins which accumulate at mitochondrial contact sites.
source: In our previously reported proteomics screen for proteins which accumulate at mitochondrial contact sites we identified a protein exhibiting the same distribution as the subunits of the MICOS complex (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from a proteomics screen and is referenced to Figure 1A showing the distribution pattern.

claim: The protein identified in the proteomics screen is the product of the gene AIM24 (systematic name YJR080C).
source: The MS/MS data identified it as the product of the gene AIM24 (systematic name YJR080C).
evidence: MS/MS data provided direct identification of the protein.

claim: AIM24 was previously found in a screen for mutants with altered inheritance of mitochondria.
source: This gene had previously been found in a screen for mutants with altered inheritance of mitochondria (Hess et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work by Hess et al., 2009.

claim: AIM24 encodes a 391 amino acid protein with a molecular weight of 44.4 kDa.
source: It encodes a 391 amino acid protein (44.4 kDa) with unknown function.
evidence: The protein size is derived from the gene sequence analysis.

claim: Aim24 was localized to mitochondria in the MitoGFP database.
source: It was localized to mitochondria in the MitoGFP database (Huh et al., 2003) and in a proteomics screen for identification of mitochondrial proteins (Reinders et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to the MitoGFP database and a proteomics screen.

claim: The deduced amino acid sequence of Aim24 predicts the presence of an N-terminal mitochondrial targeting signal.
source: The presence of an N-terminal mitochondrial targeting signal is predicted by the deduced amino acid sequence.
evidence: The prediction is based on computational analysis of the amino acid sequence.

claim: N-terminally His-tagged Aim24 shows the same apparent size as wild type Aim24 in isolated mitochondria, indicating cleavage of the targeting sequence.
source: In isolated mitochondria N-terminally His-tagged Aim24 showed the same apparent size as wild type Aim24 indicating cleavage of the targeting sequence.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data comparing protein sizes and inferring cleavage.

claim: C-terminally His-tagged Aim24 is slightly larger than wild type Aim24 as it contains the C-terminal His-tag.
source: In contrast, C-terminally His-tagged Aim24 was slightly larger as it contained the C-terminal His-tag (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The processing of the N-terminus of Aim24 strongly suggests import via the TOM-TIM23 pathway.
source: The processing of the N-terminus of Aim24 strongly suggests import via the TOM-TIM23 pathway and the location of the mature protein in the matrix space or inner membrane.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed N-terminal processing and established knowledge of mitochondrial import pathways.

claim: The C-terminus of Aim24 is located in the matrix or in the membrane.
source: In order to analyse the location of the C-terminus, we treated mitochondria and mitoplasts containing a version of Aim24 carrying a C-terminal HA-tag with proteinase K. Removal of the HA-tag was not observed, suggesting also the presence of the C-terminus in the matrix or in the membrane.
evidence: The claim is based on proteinase K protection assay data and inference about protein topology.

claim: Aim24 could only be degraded by proteinase K when mitochondria were lysed with Triton X-100.
source: Aim24 could only be degraded by proteinase K (Figure 1C,D) and several other proteases (not shown) when mitochondria were lysed with Triton X-100.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: Aim24 is resistant to alkaline extraction at pH up to 12.
source: To test whether Aim24 is firmly associated with the membrane we performed treatment of mitochondria with alkaline solutions of pH up to 12 (Figure 1D). The protein was found to be resistant against alkaline extraction.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The sequence of Aim24 does not contain a predicted transmembrane segment.
source: This observation was rather surprising, since the sequence of Aim24 does not contain a predicted transmembrane segment, although a segment lacking charged residues (residues 200–213) is present.
evidence: The claim is based on computational sequence analysis.

claim: Aim24 contains a segment lacking charged residues (residues 200–213).
source: This observation was rather surprising, since the sequence of Aim24 does not contain a predicted transmembrane segment, although a segment lacking charged residues (residues 200–213) is present.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence analysis data.

claim: The G207R, G208E mutation in Aim24 strongly reduces the hydrophobicity of the uncharged segment according to computational analysis.
source: To investigate whether Aim24 is anchored in the inner membrane by this segment, we introduced two charged residues (G207R, G208E); according to computational analysis this strongly reduces the hydrophobicity.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of the mutated sequence.

claim: The G207R, G208E mutation in Aim24 did not interfere with targeting of the protein to mitochondria in vivo.
source: This mutation did not interfere with targeting of the protein to mitochondria in vivo nor did it alter its lack of extractability by alkaline solutions (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The G207R, G208E mutation in Aim24 did not alter its lack of extractability by alkaline solutions.
source: This mutation did not interfere with targeting of the protein to mitochondria in vivo nor did it alter its lack of extractability by alkaline solutions (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: After alkaline treatment of mitochondria, the mutated Aim24 (G207R, G208E) remained in the membrane and was not present as an aggregate.
source: Moreover, after alkaline treatment of mitochondria, the mutated Aim24 remained in the membrane and was not present as an aggregate as shown by membrane flotation (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane flotation data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: In homologs of Aim24 from Kluyveromyces lactis and Candida glabrata, the uncharged segment corresponding to residues 200–213 of S. cerevisiae Aim24 is shorter with 12 and 9 residues, respectively.
source: Interestingly, in homologs of Aim24 of other species, for example Kluyveromyces lactis and Candida glabrata, the uncharged segment corresponding to residues 200–213 of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Aim24 was even shorter with 12 and 9 residues, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence comparison data from different species.

claim: Aim24 must be integrated in the mitochondrial inner membrane in a different way than by a hydrophobic α-helical transmembrane segment.
source: Thus, Aim24 must be integrated in the mitochondrial inner membrane in a different way than by a hydrophobic α-helical transmembrane segment.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental data showing membrane integration without a typical transmembrane segment.

claim: The MICOS complex is eluted early in fractions corresponding to an apparent molecular mass of ca. 1.5 MDa upon size exclusion chromatography.
source: The MICOS complex was eluted early in fractions corresponding to an apparent molecular mass of ca. 1.5 MDa.
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data.

claim: Minor fractions of Mic10 and Mic26 are found in distinct complexes of smaller size of ca. 250–300 kDa.
source: In addition, minor fractions of Mic10 and Mic26 were found in distinct complexes of smaller size of ca. 250–300 kDa.
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data.

claim: Aim24 is mainly present in fractions corresponding to 400 kDa upon size exclusion chromatography.
source: Aim24 was mainly present in fractions corresponding to 400 kDa (Figure 2A), suggesting that it is not an integral or firmly attached part of the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Aim24 is not an integral or firmly attached part of the MICOS complex.
source: Aim24 was mainly present in fractions corresponding to 400 kDa (Figure 2A), suggesting that it is not an integral or firmly attached part of the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the size exclusion chromatography data.

claim: In mitochondria isolated from cells lacking Mic60 or Mic10, the MICOS subunit Mic26 is almost exclusively found in smaller complexes of ca. 250 kDa.
source: In mitochondria isolated from cells lacking Mic60 or Mic10, the MICOS subunit Mic26 was almost exclusively found in smaller complexes of ca. 250 kDa, suggesting dissociation of the MICOS complex in these strains.
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data from deletion mutants.

claim: Deletion of Mic60 or Mic10 leads to dissociation of the MICOS complex.
source: In mitochondria isolated from cells lacking Mic60 or Mic10, the MICOS subunit Mic26 was almost exclusively found in smaller complexes of ca. 250 kDa, suggesting dissociation of the MICOS complex in these strains.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the size exclusion chromatography data showing Mic26 in smaller complexes.

claim: Aim24 is still present in a complex of the same apparent molecular mass as in wild type in mitochondria from cells lacking Mic60 or Mic10.
source: In contrast, Aim24 was still present in a complex of the same apparent molecular mass as in wild type (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: Assembly of Aim24 into its complex does not depend on the integrity of the MICOS complex.
source: Thus, assembly of Aim24 into its complex does not depend on the integrity of the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Aim24 complex formation is maintained even when MICOS is disrupted.

claim: In mitochondria from Δaim24 cells, the majority of Mic10 is found as a ca. 300 kDa complex upon gel filtration.
source: Strikingly, with mitochondria from Δaim24 cells the majority of Mic10 was found as a ca.300 kDa complex, whereas only a small fraction was present in the 1.5 MDa complex upon gel filtration.
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data from Δaim24 cells.

claim: In mitochondria from Δaim24 cells, only a small fraction of Mic10 is present in the 1.5 MDa complex upon gel filtration.
source: Strikingly, with mitochondria from Δaim24 cells the majority of Mic10 was found as a ca.300 kDa complex, whereas only a small fraction was present in the 1.5 MDa complex upon gel filtration.
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data from Δaim24 cells.

claim: In mitochondria from Δaim24 cells, the subunits Mic60, Mic27 and the majority of Mic26 are still recovered in the 1.5 MDa complex.
source: The subunits Mic60, Mic27 and the majority of Mic26 were still recovered in the 1.5 MDa complex (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Absence of Aim24 either leads to loss of Mic10 from MICOS, or Mic10 remains with MICOS but is destabilized and dissociates upon solubilisation with digitonin.
source: This suggests that absence of Aim24 either leads to loss of Mic10 from MICOS, or Mic10 remains with MICOS but is destabilized and Mic10 dissociates upon solubilisation with digitonin.
evidence: The claim presents two possible interpretations of the experimental data.

claim: Expression of C-terminally His-tagged or HA-tagged forms of Aim24 has the same effect on the integrity of the MICOS complex as deletion of the AIM24 gene.
source: Notably, the expression of C-terminally His-tagged or HA-tagged forms of Aim24 had the same effect on the integrity of the MICOS complex as deletion of the AIM24 gene; it led to almost complete dissociation of Mic10 upon solublisation of mitochondria (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data comparing tagged Aim24 to Δaim24, shown in Figure 2E.

claim: C-terminal tagging of Aim24 leads to almost complete dissociation of Mic10 upon solubilisation of mitochondria.
source: Notably, the expression of C-terminally His-tagged or HA-tagged forms of Aim24 had the same effect on the integrity of the MICOS complex as deletion of the AIM24 gene; it led to almost complete dissociation of Mic10 upon solublisation of mitochondria (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: About 93% of all gold particles labeling Mic10 in Δaim24 cells are located at the inner boundary membrane (IBM).
source: Localization of Mic10 in Δaim24 cells by immuno EM analysis is shown in Figure 2F. About 93% of all gold particles were located at the IBM, of which 51% at crista junctions.
evidence: The claim is based on cryo-immunoelectron microscopy data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: 51% of gold particles labeling Mic10 at the IBM in Δaim24 cells are located at crista junctions.
source: About 93% of all gold particles were located at the IBM, of which 51% at crista junctions.
evidence: The claim is based on cryo-immunoelectron microscopy data.

claim: In wild type mitochondria, 95% of gold particles labeling Mic10 are located at the IBM and 62% of these are at crista junctions.
source: A parallel analysis of wild type mitochondria yielded 95% at the IBM and 62% of these at crista junctions.
evidence: The claim is based on cryo-immunoelectron microscopy data from wild type cells.

claim: The localization data is consistent with a continued but weaker association of Mic10 with the MICOS subunits in Δaim24 cells.
source: This does not prove, but is consistent with a continued but weaker association of Mic10 with the MICOS subunits.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the immunoelectron microscopy localization data.

claim: Functional Aim24 is required for the integrity of Mic10 into the MICOS complex.
source: In conclusion, these results suggest that functional Aim24 is required for the integrity of Mic10 into the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined experimental data showing Mic10 dissociation in the absence of functional Aim24.

claim: In cells in which the AIM24 gene was deleted, the levels of Mic10, Mic12, Mic27 and Mic26 are increased.
source: In cells in which the AIM24 gene was deleted, the expression of MICOS subunits was altered. The levels of Mic10, Mic12, Mic27 and Mic26 were increased whereas that of Mic60 was not altered (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is based on steady state protein level analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: In cells in which the AIM24 gene was deleted, the level of Mic60 is not altered.
source: The levels of Mic10, Mic12, Mic27 and Mic26 were increased whereas that of Mic60 was not altered (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is based on steady state protein level analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Deletion of Mic60 and Mic10 leads to down-regulation of the other MICOS subunits.
source: In contrast, deletion of Mic60 and Mic10 led to down-regulation of the other MICOS subunits.
evidence: The claim is based on steady state protein level analysis in deletion mutants.

claim: The level of Aim24 in cells lacking Mic60 is unchanged.
source: The level of Aim24 in cells lacking Mic60 was unchanged and slightly decreased in cells lacking Mic10.
evidence: The claim is based on steady state protein level analysis in deletion mutants.

claim: The level of Aim24 in cells lacking Mic10 is slightly decreased.
source: The level of Aim24 in cells lacking Mic60 was unchanged and slightly decreased in cells lacking Mic10.
evidence: The claim is based on steady state protein level analysis in deletion mutants.

claim: The levels of several outer membrane and inner membrane proteins (ATP4, Su e, F1β, Tim50 and Tom40) are not altered in Δaim24 cells.
source: In comparison, the levels of several OM and IM membrane proteins, ATP4, Su e, F1β, Tim50 and Tom40, were not altered (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is based on steady state protein level analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The ratio of Mic10 in the 300 kDa fractions compared to the 1.5 MDa fractions is 5.0 when normalized between wild type and Δaim24.
source: We quantified the amount of Mic10 present in wild type and Δaim24 in the 1.5 MDa (fractions 2–5) and the 300 kDa complex (fractions 16–19) in Figure 2A,D. If the amounts of Mic10 present in the 1.5 MDa fractions in wild type and Δaim24 are normalized to a ratio of 1, the ratio in the 300 kDa fractions amounts to 5.0.
evidence: The claim is based on quantification of gel filtration data from Figures 2A and 2D.

claim: The presence of Mic10 in the 300 kDa fraction is not solely due to an unassembled form of Mic10.
source: This excludes the possibility that the presence of Mic10 in the 300 kDa fraction was due or solely due to an unassembled form of Mic10.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the quantification data showing a 5-fold increase in the 300 kDa fraction.

claim: Other MICOS subunits with similar increased levels in Δaim24 mitochondria are not present as unassembled species.
source: Notably, other MICOS subunits with similar increased levels in Δaim24 mitochondria were not present as unassembled species.
evidence: The claim is based on gel filtration data showing these subunits remain in the large complex.

claim: The levels of MICOS subunits in Aim24-HA expressing cells are not altered compared to wild type.
source: Finally, we quantified the expression levels of MICOS subunits in Aim24-HA expressing cells. Here, the levels of Mic10 and the other MICOS subunits were not altered as compared to wild type (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is based on steady state protein level analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claim: In Aim24-HA expressing cells, Mic10 is observed virtually completely in the 300 kDa fraction upon gel filtration.
source: However, with these mitochondria Mic10 was observed virtually completely in the 300 kDa fraction (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The modification of Aim24 by the HA-tag leads to a destabilization of the MICOS complex.
source: This observation strongly supports the notion that the modification of Aim24 by the HA-tag, like the deletion of Aim24, leads to a destabilization of the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the gel filtration data showing Mic10 dissociation.

claim: Aim24 is important for maintaining the integrity of the MICOS complex.
source: In sum, these findings demonstrate the importance of Aim24 for maintaining the integrity of the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined experimental data showing MICOS destabilization in the absence of functional Aim24.

claim: Mic12, Mic19, Mic27, Mic26 and Mic60 can be co-isolated with Mic10 when mitochondria are lysed with digitonin.
source: While Mic12, Mic19, Mic27, Mic26 and Mic60 could be co-isolated with Mic10, no specific binding of Aim24 was detected (Figure 3, left).
evidence: The claim is based on co-isolation assay data shown in Figure 3.

claim: No specific binding of Aim24 is detected when Mic10 is co-isolated from digitonin-lysed mitochondria.
source: While Mic12, Mic19, Mic27, Mic26 and Mic60 could be co-isolated with Mic10, no specific binding of Aim24 was detected (Figure 3, left).
evidence: The claim is based on co-isolation assay data shown in Figure 3.

claim: When mitochondria are solubilized with Triton X-100, efficient co-isolation of Aim24 with Mic10 is observed.
source: However, when mitochondria were solubilized with Triton X-100, which leads to dissociation of the MICOS complex into smaller complexes, efficient co-isolation of Aim24 with Mic10 was observed (Figure 3, right).
evidence: The claim is based on co-isolation assay data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Triton X-100 leads to dissociation of the MICOS complex into smaller complexes.
source: However, when mitochondria were solubilized with Triton X-100, which leads to dissociation of the MICOS complex into smaller complexes, efficient co-isolation of Aim24 with Mic10 was observed (Figure 3, right).
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental observation that Triton X-100 treatment allows Aim24-Mic10 interaction to be detected.

claim: Aim24 and Mic10 can specifically interact depending on the state of the MICOS complex.
source: This shows that both proteins can specifically interact depending on the state of the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the differential co-isolation results with different detergents.

claim: The precise co-fractionation of Aim24 with the MICOS subunits upon fragmentation of mitochondria into small vesicles is consistent with an association of Aim24 with the MICOS complex.
source: Furthermore, the precise co-fractionation with the MICOS subunits upon fragmentation of mitochondria into small vesicles derived from contact sites is consistent with an association of Aim24 with the MICOS complex (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the co-fractionation data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Aim24 is likely to be weakly or transiently associated with the MICOS complex at mitochondrial contact sites.
source: Thus, Aim24 is likely to be weakly or transiently associated with the MICOS complex at mitochondrial contact sites, and Mic10 appears to be involved in this interaction.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined co-isolation and co-fractionation data.

claim: Mic10 appears to be involved in the interaction between Aim24 and the MICOS complex.
source: Thus, Aim24 is likely to be weakly or transiently associated with the MICOS complex at mitochondrial contact sites, and Mic10 appears to be involved in this interaction.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the co-isolation data showing Aim24-Mic10 interaction.

claim: The MICOS complex has a high propensity to fall apart upon solubilisation even with very mild detergents.
source: It should be noted in this context that the MICOS complex itself has a high propensity to fall apart upon solubilisation even with very mild detergents.
evidence: The claim is based on the general observation from the experimental data showing complex instability.

claim: Δaim24 deletion mutants grow like wild type on glucose.
source: On glucose these cells grew like wild type, whereas on non-fermentable carbon sources, such as glycerol and lactate, growth was reduced (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is based on growth assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Δaim24 deletion mutants show reduced growth on non-fermentable carbon sources such as glycerol and lactate.
source: On glucose these cells grew like wild type, whereas on non-fermentable carbon sources, such as glycerol and lactate, growth was reduced (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is based on growth assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Cells expressing His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 in the Δaim24 deletion background do not grow at all on a non-fermentable carbon source.
source: Strikingly, cells expressing His-tagged MICOS subunits Mic12 or Mic26 in the Δaim24 deletion background did not grow at all on a non-fermentable carbon source (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is based on growth assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Cells containing His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 in the presence of Aim24 display no impairment of growth.
source: This was surprising since cells containing these His-tagged proteins in the presence of Aim24 displayed no impairment of growth.
evidence: The claim is based on growth assay data comparing tagged proteins with and without Aim24.

claim: The combination of His-tagged Mic19 or Mic27 with Δaim24 deletion does not result in a synthetic lethal phenotype on non-fermentable carbon source.
source: The combination of two other His-tagged MICOS subunits, Mic19-His6 or Mic27-His6, with Δaim24 deletion did not result in a synthetic lethal phenotype on non-fermentable carbon source (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is based on growth assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In strains containing Mic12-His6 and Mic26-His6 that lack Aim24, the MICOS complex is further destabilized.
source: In the strains containing Mic12-His6 and Mic26-His6 the MICOS complex was further destabilized, whereas in the strains containing Mic19-His6 and Mic27-His6 the MICOS complex behaved like in the Δaim24 mutant containing the wild type forms of the Mic proteins (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In strains containing Mic19-His6 and Mic27-His6 that lack Aim24, the MICOS complex behaves like in the Δaim24 mutant containing wild type forms of the Mic proteins.
source: In the strains containing Mic12-His6 and Mic26-His6 the MICOS complex was further destabilized, whereas in the strains containing Mic19-His6 and Mic27-His6 the MICOS complex behaved like in the Δaim24 mutant containing the wild type forms of the Mic proteins (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Aim24 is critical for the assembly of a fully functional MICOS complex.
source: These results corroborate the conclusion of Aim24 being critical for the assembly of a fully functional MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined growth and biochemical data.

claim: Minor alterations of specific MICOS subunits alter MICOS stability such that in the absence of Aim24 mitochondria are unable to maintain respiratory growth.
source: Apparently minor alterations of specific MICOS subunits alter its stability in such a way that in the absence of Aim24 mitochondria are unable to maintain respiratory growth.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the synthetic lethal phenotype observed with tagged Mic12 and Mic26 in Δaim24 background.

claim: All strains analyzed for respiratory complexes still contain mtDNA as checked by DAPI staining.
source: This was not due to the loss of the mitochondrial genome as all strains still contained mtDNA as checked by staining with DAPI (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is based on DAPI staining data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Mitochondria isolated from Δaim24 cells harboring His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 display a drastic reduction or complete absence of respiratory supercomplexes.
source: The mitochondria isolated from these cells displayed a drastic reduction or complete absence of the respiratory supercomplexes (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is based on Blue native gel electrophoresis data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: There is a strong reduction of the steady state levels of individual respiratory chain subunits in Δaim24 cells harboring His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26.
source: There was also a strong reduction of the steady state levels of individual respiratory chain subunits and an almost complete deficiency in subunit e (Su e) of the F1FO-ATP synthase.
evidence: The claim is based on immunoblot analysis of respiratory chain subunits.

claim: There is an almost complete deficiency in subunit e (Su e) of the F1FO-ATP synthase in Δaim24 cells harboring His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26.
source: There was also a strong reduction of the steady state levels of individual respiratory chain subunits and an almost complete deficiency in subunit e (Su e) of the F1FO-ATP synthase.
evidence: The claim is based on immunoblot analysis shown in the manuscript.

claim: The individual MICOS subunits are down-regulated when Mic12 or Mic26 are His-tagged in the Δaim24 deletion background.
source: Furthermore, the individual MICOS subunits were down-regulated as well when Mic12 or Mic26 were His-tagged in the Δaim24 deletion background (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is based on steady state protein level analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: His-tagging of MICOS subunits or deletion of Aim24 alone does not show a loss of respiratory complexes.
source: Importantly, His-tagging of MICOS subunits or deletion of Aim24 alone did not show a loss of respiratory complexes, nor was this loss observed when His-tagged Mic19 or Mic27 were present in Δaim24 mitochondria.
evidence: The claim is based on Blue native gel electrophoresis data comparing different mutant combinations.

claim: Loss of respiratory complexes is not observed when His-tagged Mic19 or Mic27 are present in Δaim24 mitochondria.
source: Importantly, His-tagging of MICOS subunits or deletion of Aim24 alone did not show a loss of respiratory complexes, nor was this loss observed when His-tagged Mic19 or Mic27 were present in Δaim24 mitochondria.
evidence: The claim is based on Blue native gel electrophoresis data comparing different mutant combinations.

claim: Aim24 is important for the formation of the respiratory chain.
source: This demonstrates the importance of Aim24 for the integrity of the MICOS complex and also the joint requirement of Aim24 and intact MICOS for the formation of the respiratory chain.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined data showing respiratory complex loss only when both Aim24 and MICOS are compromised.

claim: There is a joint requirement of Aim24 and intact MICOS for the formation of the respiratory chain.
source: This demonstrates the importance of Aim24 for the integrity of the MICOS complex and also the joint requirement of Aim24 and intact MICOS for the formation of the respiratory chain.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the synthetic phenotype observed only when both Aim24 and MICOS are compromised.

claim: Mitochondria from wild type, Δaim24 and Δaim24 cells in combination with His-tagged Mic19 or Mic27 do not show a significant difference in the distribution of membrane phospholipids and ergosterol.
source: Mitochondria from wild type, Δaim24 as well as Δaim24 cells in combination with His-tagged Mic19 or Mic27 did not show a significant difference in the distribution of membrane phospholipids and ergosterol (not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on mass spectrometry analysis of membrane lipids.

claim: Mitochondria from cells lacking Aim24 and harboring His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 contain slightly increased levels of ergosterol.
source: In contrast, mitochondria from cells lacking Aim24 and harboring His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 contained slightly increased levels of ergosterol and, conspicuously, the pattern of acyl chains specifically of cardiolipin was significantly altered (Figure 6A; Table 1).
evidence: The claim is based on mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 6A and Table 1.

claim: The pattern of acyl chains specifically of cardiolipin is significantly altered in mitochondria from cells lacking Aim24 and harboring His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26.
source: In contrast, mitochondria from cells lacking Aim24 and harboring His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 contained slightly increased levels of ergosterol and, conspicuously, the pattern of acyl chains specifically of cardiolipin was significantly altered (Figure 6A; Table 1).
evidence: The claim is based on mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 6A and Table 1.

claim: There is a shift towards longer and more saturated acyl chains in cardiolipin in mitochondria from cells lacking Aim24 and harboring His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26.
source: There was a shift towards longer and more saturated acyl chains.
evidence: The claim is based on mass spectrometry analysis of cardiolipin species.

claim: Tafazzin (Taz1) is a cardiolipin transacylase.
source: Since the enzyme responsible for mediating exchange of acyl chains on cardiolipin was identified as tafazzin (Taz1) (Schlame, 2013), we checked whether deletion of Aim24 would affect this protein.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Schlame, 2013.

claim: The steady state levels of Taz1 are drastically reduced in Δaim24 cells expressing Mic12-His6 or Mic26-His6.
source: Notably, the steady state levels of Taz1 were drastically reduced in Δaim24 cells expressing Mic12-His6 or Mic26-His6, but not in Δaim24 cells expressing Mic19-His6 or Mic27-His6 (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is based on immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The steady state levels of Taz1 are not reduced in Δaim24 cells expressing Mic19-His6 or Mic27-His6.
source: Notably, the steady state levels of Taz1 were drastically reduced in Δaim24 cells expressing Mic12-His6 or Mic26-His6, but not in Δaim24 cells expressing Mic19-His6 or Mic27-His6 (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is based on immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Cells in which the subunits Mic60 and Mic10 of the MICOS complex are deleted show wild type levels of Taz1.
source: Furthermore, cells in which the subunits Mic60 and Mic10 of the MICOS complex were deleted showed wild type levels of Taz1 (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is based on immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Loss of Taz1 is not simply a consequence of the destabilization of the MICOS complex or the loss of crista junctions.
source: Thus, loss of Taz1 is not simply a consequence of the destabilization of the MICOS complex or the loss of crista junctions.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Taz1 levels are normal in Δmic60 and Δmic10 cells.

claim: Tafazzin was reported to be anchored to the inner face of the outer membrane.
source: Tafazzin was reported to be anchored to the inner face of the outer membrane.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from the literature.

claim: Upon gradient fractionation of mitochondrial membrane vesicles, tafazzin was found in inner membrane fractions as well as in fractions containing both outer and inner membranes.
source: Upon gradient fractionation of mitochondrial membrane vesicles it was also found in inner membrane fractions as well as in fractions containing both outer and inner membranes, presumably representing contacts between both membranes (Ma et al., 2004; Brandner et al., 2005; Claypool et al., 2006; Herndon et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The MICOS complex and Aim24 may not be directly involved in membrane phospholipid metabolism.
source: In summary, the MICOS complex and Aim24 may not be directly involved in membrane phospholipid metabolism, but spatially control the process of mitochondrial protein composition which in turn leads to specific changes of the lipid composition.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the data suggesting an indirect role.

claim: The MICOS complex and Aim24 spatially control the process of mitochondrial protein composition which in turn leads to specific changes of the lipid composition.
source: In summary, the MICOS complex and Aim24 may not be directly involved in membrane phospholipid metabolism, but spatially control the process of mitochondrial protein composition which in turn leads to specific changes of the lipid composition.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the combined data on protein and lipid changes.

claim: Mitochondria of Aim24 deficient cells show an increase in the number of inner membrane septae compared to wild type mitochondria upon growth on non-fermentable carbon sources.
source: Upon growth on non-fermentable carbon sources, compared to wild type mitochondria (Figure 7A, d–f), mitochondria of Aim24 deficient cells (Figure 7B, a–i) showed an increase in the number of inner membrane septae (Figure 7B, c and f) (see also Figure 2F, b–d).
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy data shown in Figures 7A, 7B, and 2F.

claim: Inner membrane septae in Aim24 deficient cells appear like cristae without rims.
source: These structures appear like cristae without rims.
evidence: The claim is based on morphological observation from electron microscopy.

claim: Inner membrane septae likely represent entire or partial separations of the matrix compartment.
source: They likely represent entire or partial separations of the matrix compartment.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the morphological appearance of septae in electron micrographs.

claim: Mitochondria of Aim24 deficient cells show a larger average size of mitochondrial profiles compared to wild type.
source: A further characteristic was the larger average size of mitochondrial profiles.
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of electron microscopy data.

claim: Large mitochondrial structures in Aim24 deficient cells occupy up to ca. 30–50% of the total cellular area in some images.
source: These mitochondria occupied up to ca. 30–50% of the total cellular area in some images.
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of electron microscopy images.

claim: Large distorted mitochondria in Aim24 deficient cells contain abundant membranes which do not have the characteristics of cristae.
source: They contained abundant membranes, which did not have the characteristics of cristae. Instead, they were completely irregular, sheet or tube like.
evidence: The claim is based on morphological observation from electron microscopy.

claim: In giant distorted mitochondria of Aim24 deficient cells, the number, length and shape of cristae are reduced.
source: Whereas smaller sized mitochondrial profiles showed regular cristae, in the giant distorted mitochondria their number as well as the length and shape was reduced.
evidence: The claim is based on morphological observation from electron microscopy.

claim: Cells grown on fermentable carbon source show a drastic increase in the number of septae compared to wild type.
source: Cells grown on fermentable carbon source showed a drastic increase, as compared to wild type, in the number of septae (Figure 7A, a–c and Figure 7B, j–o; Table 2).
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy data shown in Figures 7A, 7B and quantified in Table 2.

claim: No other significant changes in size and shape of mitochondrial profiles are recognized in Δaim24 cells grown on fermentable carbon source.
source: No other significant changes in size and shape of mitochondrial profiles were recognized in these cells.
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy analysis of cells grown on glucose.

claim: When Δaim24 deletion strain is grown on glucose, mitochondrial morphology appears essentially as in wild type.
source: When the Δaim24 deletion strain was grown on glucose mitochondrial morphology appeared essentially as in wild type.
evidence: The claim is based on fluorescence microscopy observation.

claim: When Δaim24 cells are grown on glycerol, ca. 30% of all cells contain large mitochondrial structures.
source: However, when these cells were grown on glycerol ca. 30% of all cells contained large mitochondrial structures (Figure 7C), indicating that Aim24 is required for maintenance of normal mitochondrial morphology under respiratory conditions.
evidence: The claim is based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Aim24 is required for maintenance of normal mitochondrial morphology under respiratory conditions.
source: However, when these cells were grown on glycerol ca. 30% of all cells contained large mitochondrial structures (Figure 7C), indicating that Aim24 is required for maintenance of normal mitochondrial morphology under respiratory conditions.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation of abnormal mitochondrial structures in Δaim24 cells grown on glycerol.

claim: Mitochondria of cells in which the AIM24 gene was deleted and the MICOS complex destabilized due to the presence of His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 display virtually complete absence of cristae.
source: We further analyzed the mitochondria of cells in which the AIM24 gene was deleted and in addition the MICOS complex destabilized due to the presence of Mic12 or Mic26 as His-tagged versions. These mitochondria displayed virtually complete absence of cristae.
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy analysis of double mutant cells.

claim: Mitochondria of Δaim24 cells with His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 appear either empty or contain septae and onion-like structures.
source: They appeared either empty or septae and onion-like structures were present.
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy observation.

claim: Mitochondrial profiles in Δaim24 cells with His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 are small, and giant mitochondria are completely absent.
source: Mitochondrial profiles were small, and giant mitochondria were completely absent.
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy analysis.

claim: In cells in which MICOS subunits Mic19 or Mic27 are present in His-tagged form in combination with the Δaim24 deletion, mitochondria are indistinguishable from mitochondria of cells in which only the AIM24 gene was deleted.
source: In contrast, in cells in which MICOS subunits Mic19 or Mic27 were present in His-tagged form in combination with the Δaim24 deletion mitochondria were indistinguishable from mitochondria of cells in which only the AIM24 gene was deleted (Figure 8; Table 3).
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy data shown in Figure 8 and quantified in Table 3.

claim: Aim24, in an intricate interplay with the MICOS complex, acts as an important modulator in building the architecture and influencing function and integrity of the mitochondria.
source: We conclude that Aim24, in an intricate interplay with the MICOS complex, acts as an important modulator in building the architecture and influencing function and integrity of the mitochondria.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the combined experimental data showing Aim24's effects on MICOS, mitochondrial structure, and function.

claim: Computational structure prediction of Aim24 indicates that it belongs to the family of TRAP-like proteins.
source: Computational structure prediction of Aim24 indicates that it belongs to the family of TRAP-like proteins.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of the Aim24 sequence.

claim: A hallmark of the TRAP-like protein family is that its members are composed of antiparallel β-sheets.
source: A hallmark of this family is that its members are composed of antiparallel β-sheets (Antson et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Antson et al., 1995 and represents established knowledge.

claim: No protein with a domain consisting of β-sheets has been described to exist in the inner membrane of mitochondria.
source: So far no protein with a domain consisting of β-sheets has been described to exist in the inner membrane of mitochondria; however, it cannot be excluded that Aim24 is embedded in the lipid environment by this structural element.
evidence: The claim is based on a review of existing literature and represents current knowledge.

claim: It cannot be excluded that Aim24 is embedded in the lipid environment by a β-sheet structural element.
source: So far no protein with a domain consisting of β-sheets has been described to exist in the inner membrane of mitochondria; however, it cannot be excluded that Aim24 is embedded in the lipid environment by this structural element.
evidence: The claim is speculative, acknowledging a possibility not yet proven.

claim: Members of the TRAP-like protein family form oligomers.
source: At the same time, this might explain the existence of Aim24 as a large complex of ca. 400 kDa as the members of the TRAP-like protein family were reported to form oligomers.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about TRAP-like proteins from the literature.

claim: The existence of Aim24 as a large complex of ca. 400 kDa might be explained by oligomerization, as members of the TRAP-like protein family form oligomers.
source: At the same time, this might explain the existence of Aim24 as a large complex of ca. 400 kDa as the members of the TRAP-like protein family were reported to form oligomers.
evidence: The claim is an inference connecting the observed complex size with known properties of TRAP-like proteins.

claim: The important role of Aim24 is due to its intimate relationship to the MICOS complex.
source: The important role of Aim24 is due to its intimate relationship to the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined experimental data showing Aim24's effects on MICOS.

claim: In the absence of functional Aim24, the MICOS complex is destabilized as demonstrated by the dissociation of Mic10 upon detergent solubilisation of mitochondria.
source: In the absence of functional Aim24, the MICOS complex is destabilized as demonstrated by the dissociation of Mic10 upon detergent solubilisation of mitochondria.
evidence: The claim is based on size exclusion chromatography data showing Mic10 dissociation.

claim: In intact mitochondria, Aim24 is apparently associated with the MICOS complex.
source: In the intact mitochondria Aim24 is apparently associated with the MICOS complex, in consistence with its topology indicated by our quantitative proteomics screen (Harner et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the co-fractionation data and is consistent with previous proteomics results.

claim: The interaction between Aim24 and MICOS is highly sensitive to minor disturbances such as lysis of mitochondrial membranes even with mild detergents.
source: This interaction is obviously highly sensitive to minor disturbances, such as lysis of mitochondrial membranes even with mild detergents and the presence of C-terminal tags on certain MICOS subunits.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that the interaction is lost upon detergent treatment.

claim: The interaction between Aim24 and MICOS is sensitive to the presence of C-terminal tags on certain MICOS subunits.
source: This interaction is obviously highly sensitive to minor disturbances, such as lysis of mitochondrial membranes even with mild detergents and the presence of C-terminal tags on certain MICOS subunits.
evidence: The claim is based on the observation that C-terminal tagging of Aim24 or certain MICOS subunits affects complex stability.

claim: The interaction between Aim24 and MICOS is reflected in the strong alteration of the expression levels of the MICOS subunits in cells deficient in Aim24.
source: The interaction is also reflected in the strong alteration of the expression levels of the MICOS subunits in cells deficient in Aim24, most of them being up-regulated.
evidence: The claim is based on steady state protein level analysis showing altered MICOS subunit levels.

claim: Aim24 is likely to regulate the association of Mic10 with other subunits of the MICOS complex.
source: Thus, Aim24 is likely to regulate the association of Mic10 with other subunits of the complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Mic10 dissociates from MICOS in the absence of functional Aim24.

claim: The possibility that Aim24 exerts its function as an assembly factor of the MICOS complex cannot be excluded.
source: One would, however, not exclude the possibility that Aim24 exerts its function also as an assembly factor of the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is speculative, acknowledging an alternative or additional function for Aim24.

claim: Deletion of Aim24 leads to distinct functional deficiencies of the mitochondria.
source: Deletion of Aim24 leads to distinct functional deficiencies of the mitochondria.
evidence: The claim is based on the combined data showing growth defects and respiratory deficiencies.

claim: Aim24 deficient cells are restricted in their growth on non-fermentable carbon source.
source: In agreement with the reported alteration of inheritance of mitochondria (Hess et al., 2009), Aim24 deficient cells are restricted in their growth on non-fermentable carbon source.
evidence: The claim is based on growth assay data and is consistent with previous findings.

claim: Combination of deletion of Aim24 with the expression of His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 leads to synthetic lethality on non-fermentable carbon sources.
source: Interestingly, combination of deletion of Aim24 with the expression of each of the two MICOS subunits Mic12 or Mic26 as C-terminally His-tagged variants leads to synthetic lethality on non-fermentable carbon sources.
evidence: The claim is based on growth assay data showing no growth on non-fermentable carbon sources.

claim: The synthetic lethality points to a functional interaction of AIM24 with MIC12 and MIC26 genes.
source: This points to a functional interaction of these genes as the single deletion mutants are either not at all or only mildly affected (Harner et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the genetic interaction data and is supported by a citation.

claim: Aim24 has a very important role in controlling the function of the MICOS complex.
source: This supports the conclusion that Aim24 has a very important role in controlling the function of the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the synthetic lethal phenotype and other functional data.

claim: Aim24 is a protein with a distinct architectural role.
source: Aim24 is a protein with a distinct architectural role.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined data showing effects on mitochondrial structure.

claim: The percentage of mitochondria with septae is strongly increased in Δaim24 cells grown on fermentable and non-fermentable carbon source.
source: First, the percentage of mitochondria with septae is strongly increased, as seen in cells grown on fermentable and non-fermentable carbon source.
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative electron microscopy analysis.

claim: Giant distorted mitochondria accumulate with irregular inner membranes in Δaim24 cells.
source: And second, giant distorted mitochondria accumulate with irregular inner membranes.
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy observation.

claim: The formation of inner membrane septae indicates a role of Aim24 in the shaping of crista junctions.
source: In particular the formation of inner membrane septae indicates a role of Aim24 in the shaping of crista junctions.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the morphological changes observed in Δaim24 cells.

claim: Crista junctions are usually narrow ring- or slot-like structures.
source: These are usually narrow ring- or slot-like structures (Mannella et al., 2001; Rabl et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations and represents established knowledge.

claim: Extension of crista junctions leads to structures which in sections show double membranes crossing the matrix completely, appearing as septae.
source: Their extension leads to structures which in sections show double membranes crossing the matrix completely, and which appear as septae.
evidence: The claim is an inference about the structural relationship between extended junctions and septae.

claim: The width of the junctions of cristae and septae at the inner boundary membrane in Δaim24 cells is like in wild type.
source: Notably, the width of the junctions of cristae and septae at the inner boundary membrane were like in wild type, whereas their lateral extension was strongly increased.
evidence: The claim is based on morphological analysis from electron microscopy.

claim: The lateral extension of junctions of cristae and septae at the inner boundary membrane in Δaim24 cells is strongly increased.
source: Notably, the width of the junctions of cristae and septae at the inner boundary membrane were like in wild type, whereas their lateral extension was strongly increased.
evidence: The claim is based on morphological analysis from electron microscopy.

claim: The formation of giant mitochondria is apparent both in fluorescent and electron microscopic images of Δaim24 cells.
source: The formation of giant mitochondria is apparent both in fluorescent and electron microscopic images.
evidence: The claim is based on microscopy data from both fluorescence and electron microscopy.

claim: Giant mitochondria in Δaim24 cells show a dramatically altered structure of their inner membrane.
source: These mitochondria show a dramatically altered structure of their inner membrane.
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy observation.

claim: Giant mitochondria likely represent later stages of inner membrane deterioration concomitant with accumulation of inner membrane defects.
source: We consider it likely that they represent later stages of inner membrane deterioration concomitant with accumulation of inner membrane defects.
evidence: The claim is speculative, representing an interpretation of the morphological observations.

claim: Introducing His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 into Δaim24 cells leads to the absence of the large and giant mitochondria typical of Δaim24 cells.
source: The effect of tagging specifically the MICOS subunits Mic12 or Mic26 in the Δaim24 deletion background is dramatic. Introducing one of these altered subunits into Δaim24 cells leads to the absence of the large and giant mitochondria typical of Δaim24 cells and presence of particularly small mitochondria, entirely lacking cristae and instead containing septae.
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy analysis of double mutant cells.

claim: Introducing His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 into Δaim24 cells leads to presence of particularly small mitochondria entirely lacking cristae and instead containing septae.
source: Introducing one of these altered subunits into Δaim24 cells leads to the absence of the large and giant mitochondria typical of Δaim24 cells and presence of particularly small mitochondria, entirely lacking cristae and instead containing septae.
evidence: The claim is based on electron microscopy analysis of double mutant cells.

claim: The loss of respiratory complexes in Δaim24 cells with His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 is accompanied by the loss of complexes and components of oxidative phosphorylation.
source: This is accompanied by the loss of complexes and components of oxidative phosphorylation and the inviability under respiratory conditions.
evidence: The claim is based on Blue native gel electrophoresis and immunoblot data.

claim: The overall levels of cardiolipin and of other membrane phospholipids are not altered in Δaim24 cells with His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26.
source: Although the over all levels of cardiolipin and of other membrane phospholipids is not altered in these latter mutants, the difference in the pattern of acyl chains in cardiolipin is remarkable.
evidence: The claim is based on mass spectrometry analysis of membrane lipids.

claim: The difference in the pattern of acyl chains in cardiolipin is remarkable in Δaim24 cells with His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26.
source: Although the over all levels of cardiolipin and of other membrane phospholipids is not altered in these latter mutants, the difference in the pattern of acyl chains in cardiolipin is remarkable.
evidence: The claim is based on mass spectrometry analysis of cardiolipin species.

claim: The massive reduction of respiratory complexes whose function is dependent on cardiolipin indicates a connection between Aim24, cardiolipin and the function of the MICOS complex.
source: The massive reduction of respiratory complexes whose function is dependent on cardiolipin indicates a connection between Aim24, cardiolipin and the function of the MICOS complex.
evidence: The claim is an inference connecting the observed respiratory defects with cardiolipin changes.

claim: The alteration in the types of acyl residues in cardiolipin observed in Δaim24 cells with His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 are characteristic of those described for mutants with deficiencies in tafazzin in different organisms.
source: Surprisingly, the alteration in the types of acyl residues observed were characteristic of those described for mutants with deficiencies in tafazzin in different organisms (Vreken et al., 2000; Schlame et al., 2002; Gu et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison with published data on tafazzin mutants, supported by citations.

claim: Deficiency in tafazzin underlies the Barth syndrome, a severe X-chromosome-linked disorder characterized by cardiac and skeletal myopathy and neutropenia.
source: Deficiency in tafazzin underlies the Barth syndrome, a severe X-chromosome-linked disorder characterized by cardiac and skeletal myopathy and neutropenia (Barth et al., 1983).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation and represents established medical knowledge.

claim: In mitochondria of Barth syndrome patient cells, the fraction of cardiolipin with tetralinoleoyl groups is largely diminished.
source: In mitochondria of patient cells the fraction of cardiolipin with tetralinoleoyl groups is largely diminished.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Barth syndrome from the literature.

claim: Alterations of the structure of cristae and partial deficiency of respiratory complexes were observed in humans and also in several different organisms including yeast with tafazzin deficiency.
source: Furthermore, alterations of the structure of cristae and partial deficiency of respiratory complexes were observed in humans and also in several different organisms including yeast (Joshi et al., 2009; Acehan et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on tafazzin deficiency.

claim: Tafazzin was suggested to be recruited to non-bilayer type lipid domains that occur in curved membrane areas sensing non-bilayer arrangement of membrane lipids.
source: It was suggested to be recruited to non-bilayer type lipid domains that occur in curved membrane areas sensing non-bilayer arrangement of membrane lipids (Schlame et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Schlame et al., 2012.

claim: Mitochondrial cristae junctions and contact sites structured by the MICOS complex correspond to areas with non-bilayer arrangement of membrane lipids where tafazzin is recruited.
source: Mitochondrial cristae junctions and contact sites, structured by the MICOS complex correspond exactly to such proposed areas.
evidence: The claim is an inference connecting the structural features of crista junctions with the proposed sites of tafazzin recruitment.

claim: The human homolog of Mic26, APOOL, has the ability to bind cardiolipin.
source: Interestingly, the human homolog of Mic26, APOOL, has recently been shown to have the ability to bind cardiolipin (Weber et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Weber et al., 2013.

claim: Mitochondria lacking Aim24 and containing either His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 almost completely lack tafazzin.
source: We report here that mitochondria lacking Aim24 and containing either His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 not only show the characteristic alterations of cardiolipin resulting from tafazzin depletion, but in addition almost completely lack tafazzin.
evidence: The claim is based on immunoblot analysis showing drastically reduced Taz1 levels.

claim: The phenotype of Δaim24 cells with His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 is much more severe than that reported for tafazzin deficiency.
source: Surprisingly, beside the drastic changes in mitochondrial architecture, there is a practically complete loss of respiratory complexes. This phenotype is much more severe than that reported for tafazzin deficiency, but can be explained by the complete loss of cristae in these mutant cells.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of the observed phenotype with published data on tafazzin mutants.

claim: The severe phenotype of Δaim24 cells with His-tagged Mic12 or Mic26 can be explained by the complete loss of cristae in these mutant cells.
source: This phenotype is much more severe than that reported for tafazzin deficiency, but can be explained by the complete loss of cristae in these mutant cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference connecting the loss of cristae with the severe respiratory defect.

claim: The localization of tafazzin in the outer membrane provides it with the ability to reach the inner membrane specifically at contact sites and crista junctions.
source: Putting all the available information together we propose that the localization of tafazzin in the outer membrane provides it with the ability to reach the inner membrane specifically at contact sites and crista junctions.
evidence: The claim is a speculative proposal integrating the available data.

claim: The proposed mechanism would explain the partial co-localization of tafazzin with inner membrane fractions.
source: On the one hand, this would explain the partial co-localization with inner membrane fractions (Claypool et al., 2006; Herndon et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the proposed model and is supported by citations.

claim: Tafazzin could become enzymatically active directly at crista junctions where cardiolipin modified by tafazzin is specifically needed.
source: On the other hand in this way tafazzin could become enzymatically active directly at crista junctions, membrane sites showing extreme curvature where cardiolipin modified by tafazzin is specifically needed (Schlame et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is a speculative proposal about tafazzin function, supported by a citation.

claim: The proposed mechanism may be relevant to why and how only a specific limited fraction of cardiolipin is modified by tafazzin.
source: Such a mechanism may be relevant also in regard to the important question raised previously, why and how only a specific limited fraction of cardiolipin is modified by tafazzin (Schlame, 2013).
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a possible explanation for a previously raised question, supported by a citation.

claim: Aim24 appears to have an important role in determining mitochondrial architecture by affecting assembly of the MICOS complex.
source: In conclusion, Aim24 appears to have an important role in determining mitochondrial architecture by affecting not only assembly of the MICOS complex, but also by organizing complex reactions such as the remodelling of cardiolipin which makes it competent for the formation of respiratory supercomplexes and the architecture of cristae.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the combined experimental data.

claim: Aim24 has an important role in organizing complex reactions such as the remodelling of cardiolipin which makes it competent for the formation of respiratory supercomplexes and the architecture of cristae.
source: In conclusion, Aim24 appears to have an important role in determining mitochondrial architecture by affecting not only assembly of the MICOS complex, but also by organizing complex reactions such as the remodelling of cardiolipin which makes it competent for the formation of respiratory supercomplexes and the architecture of cristae.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the combined experimental data linking Aim24 to cardiolipin remodeling and respiratory complex formation.
